nodes.name: Nickel substrate surface activation
nodes.procedure: In order to prepare the nickel substrate surface for the composite electrodeposition, the substrates were immersed repeatedly in 1.0 M KOH, 13.2 w/v% HCl, and 5 w/v% H₂SO₄ solutions for 1 min in each one, to deoxidize and activate the surface.
nodes.source_text: the substrates were immersed repeatedly in 1.0M KOH, 13.2 w/v% HCl, and 5 w/v% H₂SO₄ solutions for 1 min in each one

nodes.name: Ni/Nb₂O₅ composite electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The composition of the composite electrodeposition bath was: 280 gL⁻¹ NiSO₄·6H₂O, 35 gL⁻¹ NiCl₂·6H₂O, and 45 gL⁻¹ H₃BO₃ to regulate the pH at a value of 3.5, with the addition of 3 gL⁻¹ of Nb₂O₅ nanoparticles. Ni/Nb₂O₅ composite electrodeposition was performed in a two-electrode cell using a nickel anode, by application of a -0.05 Acm⁻² pulse at 55°C, during 2700s. A 45 μm thickness for the entire coating is estimated [14,30].

nodes.characterization_summary: Scanning electron micrographs show rough nickel structure with Nb₂O₅ particle agglomerates on the catalyst surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Morphology and surface compositional structure were established by scanning electron micrographs of the catalyst's surface with a Supra 40 FESEM (Zeiss Company) working at 3 kV

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS measurements show about 12 at% Nb in the nickel matrix of the catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the EDS measurements (Figs. S1 and S2), the sample of Fig. 1 contains about 12% at. Nb in the nickel matrix

nodes.characterization_summary: Confocal microscopy shows RMS roughness values of 3.02, 3.36, 2.64 μm and surface area factors of 7.73, 7.97, 7.67 for catalysts in different electrolytes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Table 1 shows the results of mean square roughness and surface area factor, calculated using the LEXT OLS4100 software

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows oriented (111) and (200) planes of crystalline Ni and Nb₂O₅ reflection planes (e.g., Nb₂O₅(001) at 2θ=22.53°, d=3.94 Å) consistent across all aged catalyst samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3a shows the X-ray diffraction patterns of the Ni/Nb₂O₅ catalysts after the evaluation of the HER catalytic activity under different NaCl solutions containing different concentrations of KOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Nb₂O₅ bands at 200-300 cm⁻¹ (Nb-O-Nb bending), 660 cm⁻¹ (symmetric stretching), 900 cm⁻¹ (Nb=O), water at 1640 cm⁻¹, and NiO at ~480 and ~555 cm⁻¹; NiO peaks diminish above 5.6 wt% KOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3b shows the Raman spectra corresponding to the samples after being aged in the electrochemical experiments in the different electrolyte compositions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammograms at 5 mV s⁻¹ show HER current densities at -1.5 V vs SCE of -15.0, -10.9, -9.6 mA cm⁻² and Tafel slopes of 0.103, 0.106, 0.109 V dec⁻¹ with increasing KOH concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 5a shows the cyclic voltammograms measured at 5mVs⁻¹ and 298K on Ni/Nb₂O₅ composite electrodes in 3.43wt.% NaCl solution with different amounts of KOH (5.6 wt.%, 15 wt.%, and 30 wt.%).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS at -1.2 V vs SCE shows electrolyte resistance Rs decreasing (1.30, 0.61, 0.48 Ω cm²), charge transfer resistance Rct increasing (302.2, 557.4, 412.8 Ω cm²), and Cdl values of 1.57×10⁻⁴, 2.27×10⁻⁴, 1.69×10⁻⁴ F cm⁻² with KOH concentration for fresh catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 7b and c show the Nyquist plots obtained for the Ni/Nb₂O₅ electrodes in the different potentials used both with freshly synthesized electrodes (Fig. 7b) and after the rapid aging stage (Fig. 7c).

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-vis of aged electrolytes shows disappearing [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ absorption peak with increasing KOH concentration, indicating reduced Ni dissolution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4 shows the UV–vis spectra obtained from the electrolytes after their use for the electrochemical characterization studies of the catalysts.
